reasons: Work is not saved between page loads.
Server data is written as raw HTML.
The page-start document load can never run.
Only 22 of 35 sections were included in this review, so the later editing, validation and export parts are not covered here.

terms.meaning: values the program remembers while it runs, here workflowData and currentStep.
one stage of the guided workflow, numbered from zero.
the visual row of steps that shows which stage the user is on.
saving the finished survey to a file in a chosen format.
a plain text table format where values are separated by commas.
a simple plain text format that uses symbols for headings and lists.

depends_on: frontend/index.html (the classic page it links to)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and shared memory
sections.what: Holds the backend address, the current step number, and the in-memory record of documents, plan, questions and validation results.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the workflow's progress in one place so each step can read what earlier steps produced.
sections.watch_out: Everything here disappears on page reload.

sections.name: workflowData
sections.title: Empty workflow record
sections.what: Defines the starting shape of the workflow record with empty document list, no plan, no questions and no validation results.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a clean starting point, and startOver reuses the same shape.
sections.watch_out: Any new field must be added here and in startOver, or resets will be incomplete.

sections.name: document DOMContentLoaded handler
sections.title: Page start setup
sections.what: On load, checks backend status, starts the 30 second status timer, and would load documents if the user is past step one.
sections.why: Likely reason: same startup pattern as the classic page.
sections.watch_out: The step counter starts at zero, so the document load inside this block never runs on first load.

sections.name: checkAPIStatus
sections.title: Backend status check
sections.what: Asks the health address whether the backend is up and updates the footer badge to Online, Error or Offline.
sections.why: Likely reason: the wizard uses a dedicated health address, unlike the classic page.
sections.watch_out: Any successful response counts as online.

sections.name: startWorkflow
sections.title: Starting the workflow
sections.what: Moves the user from the welcome screen to step one.
sections.why: Likely reason: the start button needs a single named action.
sections.watch_out: None.

sections.name: nextStep
sections.title: Moving forward
sections.what: Advances to the next step, but never past step five.
sections.why: Likely reason: the last step is the final stage, so the limit prevents going beyond it.
sections.watch_out: The limit is a fixed number, so adding a step needs this changed too.

sections.name: previousStep
sections.title: Moving back
sections.what: Returns to the previous step, but never before the welcome screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user correct earlier choices.
sections.watch_out: None.

sections.name: goToStep
sections.title: Switching the visible step
sections.what: Hides the current step panel, shows the chosen one, updates the progress bar, scrolls to the top, and loads documents when step one opens.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the single place where navigation happens, so all steps behave the same.
sections.watch_out: Only step one loads documents, so other steps must load their own data.

sections.name: updateStepper
sections.title: Progress bar highlighting
sections.what: Marks the current step as active and earlier steps as completed.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the user a sense of how far they have come.
sections.watch_out: It assumes the progress items appear in the same order as the step numbers.

sections.name: startOver
sections.title: Starting over
sections.what: After a confirmation prompt, clears all stored work and returns to the welcome screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user begin a new survey without reloading the page.
sections.watch_out: Typed text in form fields and displayed results are not cleared, only the stored data.

sections.name: openClassicUI
sections.title: Switching to the classic page
sections.what: Opens the classic index page in the same window.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets users who prefer the single-page tool switch.
sections.watch_out: Stored work is lost when leaving this page.

sections.name: showLoading
sections.title: Loading indicator
sections.what: Shows the full-screen spinner with a chosen message, updating the message text if that element exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells the user what is happening during long calls such as planning.
sections.watch_out: The overlay itself is looked up without a check, so a missing overlay causes an error.

sections.name: hideLoading
sections.title: Hiding the loading indicator
sections.what: Removes the spinner after a request finishes.
sections.why: Likely reason: pairs with the show function.
sections.watch_out: None.

sections.name: showError
sections.title: Error display
sections.what: Turns errors into readable text and shows them in the chosen area in red.
sections.why: Likely reason: different error shapes need one display.
sections.watch_out: The message is inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: handleFileUpload (part 1)
sections.title: Choosing and sending documents
sections.what: Reads the selected files and document type, then uploads each file one at a time and collects successes and failures.
sections.why: Likely reason: one failing file should not stop the rest.
sections.watch_out: Long lists of files keep the spinner up for a long time.

sections.name: handleFileUpload (part 2)
sections.title: Showing upload results
sections.what: Lists uploaded files with their IDs and failed files with reasons, resets the form, and reloads the document list.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives clear per-file feedback before the user moves on.
sections.watch_out: Failure reasons from the server are inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: loadDocuments
sections.title: Loading the document list
sections.what: Asks the backend for uploaded documents and stores them, then displays them.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the list current after each upload.
sections.watch_out: Errors appear inside the list as raw HTML.

sections.name: displayDocuments
sections.title: Drawing document cards
sections.what: Creates a card per document with title, type, audience labels, version and upload date.
sections.why: Likely reason: a readable summary of what the user has uploaded.
sections.watch_out: Titles are inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: handlePlanSurvey (part 1)
sections.title: Requesting the survey plan
sections.what: Reads the goal, audience, required topics and model type, sends them to the planning endpoint, and shows the planned questions.
sections.why: Likely reason: the planning step turns the goal into questions, which later steps use.
sections.watch_out: Planned text from the backend is inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: handlePlanSurvey (part 2)
sections.title: Showing plan and saving questions
sections.what: Builds the plan cards, stores the planned questions for later steps, and shows the result or the raw data if the format is unexpected.
sections.why: Likely reason: saving the questions here is what makes the review step possible.
sections.watch_out: If the backend does not send a questions list, the review step has nothing to show.

sections.name: acceptPlanAndContinue
sections.title: Accepting the plan
sections.what: If questions exist, builds the review list and moves to step three, otherwise asks the user to plan first.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops the user from reviewing an empty list.
sections.watch_out: It checks only that questions exist, not that the plan is valid.

sections.name: displayQuestionsForReview
sections.title: Building the review list
sections.what: Draws one card per question with its number, type, category, options and reasoning, plus Edit and Delete buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user check and change each question before validation. The Edit and Delete functions are defined in a part of the file not included in this review.
sections.watch_out: Buttons refer to questions by position, so removing one can shift the positions the other buttons use, and the delete logic is not visible here. Question text is inserted as raw HTML.

sections.name: editQuestion
sections.title: Edit question placeholder
sections.what: Shows a message that question editing is not built yet. Clicking edit does not change any question.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder for a feature that has not been written yet.
sections.watch_out: Users may expect edits that never happen, because nothing is saved.

sections.name: deleteQuestion
sections.title: Delete question after confirmation
sections.what: Asks the user to confirm, then removes the chosen question from the working question list and redraws the review list.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The confirmation likely prevents accidental deletes.
sections.watch_out: Removes the question only from workflowData.questions, so the saved survey plan may still contain it and the JSON export can still include it.

sections.name: proceedToValidation
sections.title: Move to validation after check
sections.what: Blocks the move to the Validate step with a message when there are no questions. Otherwise it jumps to step 4.
sections.why: Stops users from validating an empty survey.
sections.watch_out: The step number 4 is fixed in this function, so reordering the steps means changing it too.

sections.name: runValidation (part 1)
sections.title: Start validation and build results
sections.what: Sends the survey plan to the backend validation endpoint and starts building the results panel from the hard checks. Stops with a message if no plan exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: the plan must exist first, and the backend does the actual checking.
sections.watch_out: Issue text from the server is placed into the page as HTML without escaping, so any markup in it will be shown or run.

sections.name: runValidation (part 2)
sections.title: Show quality scores and suggestions
sections.what: Adds color-coded quality scores out of 10 and suggestions to the results, then enables the Continue to Export button and hides the spinner. If the request fails, it shows an error in the results panel.
sections.why: Lets users see which quality areas need work at a glance. Scores are advice, and hard checks are the required ones.
sections.watch_out: The Continue to Export button is enabled even when the hard checks failed, and the scores are colored by fixed cutoffs of 7 and 5.

sections.name: exportSurvey
sections.title: Choose export format and download
sections.what: Builds the file content for JSON, CSV, or Markdown and starts a download with a timestamped file name. Any other format shows a not-implemented message.
sections.why: One entry point so every export button uses the same steps.
sections.watch_out: JSON comes from the survey plan, while CSV and Markdown use the working question list, so the files can disagree after edits.

sections.name: convertToCSV
sections.title: Turn questions into spreadsheet rows
sections.what: Builds a CSV file with a header row and one row per question containing its text, type, and category. Double quotes in the question text are doubled so the file stays valid.
sections.why: Quoting keeps commas and quote marks inside question text from breaking the columns.
sections.watch_out: Only the question text is escaped, so a type or category value containing a double quote would break the file.

sections.name: convertToMarkdown
sections.title: Turn plan into readable document
sections.what: Builds a Markdown document with the survey title, description, and each question with its type, category, options, and reasoning.
sections.why: Gives a human-readable copy for documentation.
sections.watch_out: The questions come from the working list rather than the plan, so this document may not match the JSON export.

sections.name: downloadFile
sections.title: Save text as file in browser
sections.what: Wraps the content in a file, creates a temporary link to it, clicks the link to start the download, then removes the link and the temporary address.
sections.why: A browser cannot save a file directly from script, so a hidden link is used.
sections.watch_out: This only works inside a browser. The file name is used exactly as the caller gives it.

sections.name: downloadJSON
sections.title: Download plan as JSON file
sections.what: Saves the current survey plan as a JSON file. The file name starts with the label passed in, such as planner, plus a timestamp. Shows a message if there is no plan.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shortcut for the plan download button on the planning step.
sections.watch_out: It repeats the download steps from the file download function instead of reusing them, so a fix in one place may be missed in the other.

sections.name: viewDashboard
sections.title: Dashboard placeholder message
sections.what: Shows a coming soon message. No dashboard exists yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder for a future feature.
sections.watch_out: Anything that links here will look like a working feature to users.

sections.name: closeModal
sections.title: Hide a popup by its id
sections.what: Hides the popup with the given id by setting its display to none.
sections.why: Reusable, so every popup closes the same way.
sections.watch_out: Fails with an error if no element has that id.

sections.name: showQuickTour
sections.title: Open the quick tour popup
sections.what: Shows the element with id tourModal as a flex box.
sections.why: Likely reason: a help popup that was planned, or removed from the page.
sections.watch_out: The tourModal element does not appear in wizard.html as provided, so clicking the tour link would cause an error.

summary: Browser logic for the step-by-step version of the research tool, which walks the user through upload, planning, reviewing questions, validating and exporting a survey.
purpose: Moves the user through numbered steps and keeps the work done so far in memory.
why: Likely reason: a guided flow suits users new to survey design. Reason not stated in the code.
how: On load it checks backend status. The step functions show the right panel and update the progress bar. Upload, planning and review functions call the backend and store results in workflowData. Later steps for review editing, validation, exporting and the dashboard are defined below the reviewed part.
inputs: Form input, selected files, button clicks, and answers from the backend.
outputs: Updated step panels, a progress indicator, stored data for later steps, and downloads.
risks: All work is held only in memory, so a reload loses it. Server text is written as raw HTML. The initial document load on page start is never reached because the step counter starts at zero.
debug: If a step does not appear, check that goToStep finds an element named with the step number. If progress is lost after reload, this is expected because nothing is saved. If the review step is empty, confirm the plan step stored questions.
